title: Capacity Sentinel: burst-tolerant micro-rightsizer and per-tenant utilization narratives
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Our Dedicated fleet customers request predictable throughput and cost efficiency during uneven, bursty traffic patterns. Current bulk rightsizers average over long windows and miss short burst requirements; teams either overcommit (wasted cost) or underprovision (SLO violations). Goal: build a 'Capacity Sentinel' micro-rightsizer that produces per-tenant, SLO-aware capacity recommendations that preserve burst headroom and produce human-readable utilization narratives for Console and Billing teams. The system should be conservative by default, simulate impact, and export actionable runbooks for operators and finance.

Scope and deliverables: 1) Ingest 90-day, 7-day, and 1-hour telemetry windows (QPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, queue depth, error rate) and tenant SLA definitions. 2) Build a burst-aware headroom model that estimates required committed slots for target SLOs with burst retention (configurable tolerance percentiles). 3) Generate per-tenant narratives (short plain-text summaries) explaining utilization patterns, suggested commit delta, expected monthly cost delta, risk level, and recommended autoscale policy (min/max/burst-buffer). 4) Add a Console panel to preview recommendations, run simulated canaries, and export CSV/PDF for finance. 5) Provide an API endpoint for programmatic pulls and a lightweight scan job to generate weekly emails for high-impact tenants.

Technical approach: - Data pipeline: incremental consumer from metrics store (Influx/Prometheus) + recent request traces to estimate tail-behavior during bursts. - Modeling: combine fast heuristics (EWMA + max-window) with a lightweight probabilistic tail estimator to quantify burst probability and required slot headroom. - Recommendation logic: convert slots -> cost using rate-card, simulate 30/90/365-day scenarios, and present both conservative and aggressive option tiers. - UX: one-line narrative + three action buttons (Apply, Schedule Canary, Export). - Safety: implement canary checks (synthetic traffic replay at 20% of suggested delta) and automatic rollback on SLO regressions.

Trade-offs: - Accuracy vs. compute: heavier probabilistic models increase CPU in Planner; use tiered approach (fast heuristics for most tenants, probabilistic only for high-impact ones). - Conservative defaults vs. saving: default to preserve SLOs; add an ‘aggressive’ mode for customers who opt-in. - Visibility: narratives must be succinct for finance while containing links to deep telemetry for operators.

Success metrics (KPIs): - Reduce average committed cost for pilot customers by >=12% without increased SLO violations. - 95% of simulated canary runs pass latency p99 SLOs. - Avg time-to-action for recommended commits < 7 days (from alert to applied commit).

Monitoring & rollout: phased rollout: 1) internal pilot on non-production tenants, 2) opt-in pilot with 5 production tenants, 3) wider availability behind feature flag. Monitoring dashboards: recommendation accuracy, canary pass rates, delta cost realized, and false-positive/negative rates.

Open questions: - What is the canonical rate-card source for cost estimates? (Finance input required) - How many tenants qualify as "high-impact" to justify probabilistic modeling? - Should recommendations be auto-applied for customers on managed plans?

Stakeholders: Product: Sofia Martinez; Console: Ethan Brooks; Data Platform: Priya Nair; Finance: Liam O'Connor; SRE: Rashid Khan.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry ingestion covers 90d/7d/1h windows with documented schema and backfill strategy
Burst-aware model produces slot recommendations and simulated cost deltas for 95% of tenants in pilot
Console displays per-tenant narrative, simulated canary runner, and CSV export
Canary runner validates against p50/p95/p99 SLOs and supports automatic rollback
Weekly scan job emails top-20 high-impact recommendation summaries to configured contacts
